newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged ahead of MAC deal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - unchanged ahead of MAC deal.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were unchanged on the day, as players prepared for the largest issue of the week Wednesday combined with key inflation data.
One market analyst said despite the overall flat secondary market, certain sectors showed unexpected strength. He pointed in particular to bank qualified bonds and to triple-A, long-term bonds.

Morgan Stanley & Co plans to price a $579 million Municipal Assistance Corp for the City of New York issue Wednesday, after a two-day retail order period. To see the retail scale, double click on nN10220303.
In the muni secondary, bids remained unchanged at 5.73 percent on Chicago Skyway MBIA 5-1/2s of 2023. Yields were alos unchanged, at 5.58 percent, on Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5-1/4s of 2023.
Futures ended virtually unchanged, as the March municipal contract held steady at 116-12/32 and March T-bonds lost 2/32 to 114-12/32. The MOB spread widened two ticks from Monday to 64 ticks.
Underwriters raised yields on some of the day's larger new issues, including Connecticut's $112 million housing bond issue.
PaineWebber increased yields five basis points several maturities, but left the top yield in 2028 unchanged at 6.071 percent. To see the repricing scale, double click on

But Lehman Brothers was able to raise prices on Orange County, Calif.'s $137 million airport revenue bond deal, cutting yields five basis points on the 2003 through 2012 maturities. To see the repricing, double click on nN10249674.

On the largest negotiated deal of the day, Texas Water Development Board's $185 million revenue bond issue, PaineWebber restructured the issue to adjust coupon rates in several maturities, but left yields unchanged nN10239086.
A key focus of the week is release of November inflation data.

The producer price index for November is set for release Wednesday at 0830 EST. Economists surveyed by Reuters expect the figure to show a 0.3 percent rise overall and 0.2 percent increase excluding food and energy.
Last month's consumer price index will come Thursday, and is also expected to show a 0.3 percent increase overall and a 0.2 percent increase at the core.
Scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $2 billion in 41 offerings for Wednesday, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
Competitive sales total $499 million in 20 issues. The largest issue is a $165 million Metro Atlanta Rapid Transit Agnecy deal at 1100 EST.
Negotiated sales total $1.5 billion in 21 offerings. The largest is a $579 million Municipal Assistance Corp for the City of New York deal through Morgan Stanley & Co.
